elaine (pm): Heads-up: I sketched a prioritization matrix for routing/residency pilots. Need product + eng to tag customers and pick pilots by Tue. https://redwood.share/notes/routing-onramp-matrix

divya (product): link looks good. I'll add FinCo and Acme rows. quick question: do we treat residency as per-route or per-customer?

oliver (sales): customers are asking per-route for auditable traffic lanes. FinCo only needs payments routes in-region; other routes OK to failover.

samir (arch): we should model residency as "route-scoped" (boolean) + isolation level: soft (affinity preferred) / hard (no cross-region). This affects KV-cache locality and model-eviction behavior.

miguel (eng): engineering note: hard isolation implies dedicated placement or strict node labeling. That will block bin packing and increase reserved capacity. I can quantify if product finalizes pilot list.

nina (sre): Ops constraints: for any pilot with hard isolation we must have synthetic checks that verify the correct region is used and an alert when fallback is triggered. Canary policy: 10% traffic, 30m stable window, p95 latency <= 2x baseline, error-rate <0.3%.

ops-bot: infra-alerts enabled for routing-policy changes.

elaine (pm): Draft prioritization columns: customer, route, isolation-level (none/preferred/hard), SLA tier, expected ARR, migration complexity (low/med/high), legal ok? Add rows by EOD Mon.

samir (arch): propose a tiny policy JSON for product to review so customers can reason about permutations:
```json
{
  "policy_name": "payments_eu",
  "match": {"customer": "FinCo", "route": "payments"},
  "isolation": "hard",
  "regions": ["eu-west-1"],
  "fallback": {"regions": [], "allowed": false}
}
```

miguel (eng): +1. Also include defaults for autoscale: min_reserved_gpus, max_burst, eviction_window. Without defaults we'll ship conservative >cost settings.

divya (product): I'll propose defaults: min_reserved_gpus=1 for hard isolation pilots, max_burst=2x, eviction_window=5m. We can adjust after sizing.

oliver (sales): Heads-up: Acme wants SLA 99.9 for their EU traffic and an audit log of routing decisions. They may sign a 12-mo commit if we can meet that.

nina (sre): Audit logs are doable but need retention SLAs and index cost. Suggest we scope a minimal audit event stream (policy_hit, chosen_region, fallback_reason) and iterate.

samir (arch): Telemetry dependency: every policy evaluation must emit policy_id + outcome. Console needs a visualization for 'policy hit rate' and 'fallbacks per hour'.

elaine (pm): New action items: 1) Product owners complete matrix by EOD Mon. 2) Eng to provide sizing + delta for hard isolation pilots (miguel, Tue). 3) SRE to draft canary/runbook + synthetic checks (nina, Tue). 4) Arch to spec minimal policy telemetry (samir, Tue). We'll review Wed sync and pick 2 pilots for Q3.

miguel (eng): I'll run a rough cost model for 3 customers (FinCo, Acme, BetaLabs) and include token cost delta + GPU footprint. ETA Tue EOD.

divya (product): Added FinCo/Acme/BetaLabs. Marked BetaLabs as low revenue but low complexity (good test).

oliver (sales): I'll prep customer comms templates that explain failover behavior and clearly label which routes are covered by residency.

samir (arch): minor callout: we should include a migration rollback knob that switches clients to global model_variant if region capacity exhausted. Policy should allow 'soft_fallback_to_model_variant' as an escape.

elaine (pm): Agreed. I'll add that to the matrix as an optional column. Last note: can we keep policy DSL human-readable for legal to review? If not, product should own a plain-language summary per policy for contracts.

nina (sre): I'll draft the runbook snippet now and attach to the doc: "canary -> monitor latency/p99,error-rate,policy-fallback-count -> if fallback_count>1 per min rollback -> page oncall"

ops-bot: deploy scheduled: policy-telemetry-proxy v0.2 -> staging (triggered by samir).

elaine (pm): Thanks all. If no blockers we'll lock pilots Wed and send customers the onramp comms.
